extracted.intended_audience: ACL Rolling Review (ARR) reviewers / conference peer reviewers in computational linguistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers participating in the ACL Rolling Review process, covering responsibilities, evaluation criteria (soundness/excitement/overall), common mistakes, paper problems to flag, and critical procedural standards (confidentiality, double-blind, AI use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate Time
rubrics_metrics.description: Block calendar time for reading assignments, writing reviews, and participating in discussion periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and reserve sufficient uninterrupted time for the full review workflow (initial read, in-depth read, writing, and later participation in discussions and response acknowledgement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment Check / Expertise & Conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify expertise match and conflicts of interest before accepting an assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm you have the necessary subject-matter expertise to judge the submission and declare any conflicts; if not appropriate, decline to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk-rejection checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete a desk-rejection checklist examining appropriateness, hallucinated references, anonymity violations, style compliance, limitations sections, and ethics concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly check whether the submission is appropriate for the venue, contains fabricated or hallucinated references, violates double-blind anonymity, fails to meet style or submission requirements, omits required limitations/negative-result discussion, or raises ethical/legal concerns that warrant desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write Strong Reviews (structured approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a structured approach to writing reviews: read papers twice, be specific with criticism, provide concrete examples, avoid common reviewer heuristics that introduce bias, ensure scores align with review content, and maintain professional, neutral tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First skim to form expectations and locate contributions; then read closely for technical details. When criticizing, point to concrete lines/experiments/claims and suggest fixes. Ensure numeric scores are justified by the review text and keep tone collegial and neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge author responses, participate in reviewer discussions, and update assessments as warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively read and consider author rebuttals and other reviewers' comments during discussion periods, and revise your evaluation if new information materially affects your judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Score reflecting technical soundness; must be justified by review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigning a low soundness score, explicitly identify the technical flaw(s) that motivate that score. Support statements about correctness, reproducibility, and methodological validity with specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excitement Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Score reflecting personal interest or excitement separate from technical quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to indicate novelty, potential impact, or personal enthusiasm, distinct from the soundness assessment. Be transparent about personal taste vs. objective concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite assessment balancing soundness, novelty, and potential impact to recommend acceptance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize soundness and excitement (and other relevant factors) into a clear recommendation; explain trade-offs and the primary reasons behind the overall judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Common Reviewer Heuristics (common review mistakes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on heuristics that can undermine review quality, such as dismissing results as unsurprising (H1), confirmation bias toward expected outcomes (H2), penalizing methodological diversity (H8, H10), demanding unnecessary experiments beyond claim scope (H13), or conflating acknowledged limitations with weaknesses (H16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of at least 17 identified heuristics. Avoid cursory dismissals, check your assumptions, and do not judge work for not doing work it never claimed to do. Distinguish honest limitations from fatal flaws and avoid applying inconsistent standards across submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag Methodology Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and flag methodology problems such as reproducibility failures, insufficient LLM validation, and unclear assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for missing experimental details, absent code/data/seed reporting, inadequate validation of large language model (LLM) behaviors, unclear or unstated modeling assumptions, and methods that make results non-reproducible or uninterpretable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag Sourcing and Ethics Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Spot and report sourcing issues including licensing problems and ethical concerns related to datasets, model use, or evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check dataset licenses and provenance, consent and privacy issues, potential misuse risks, and whether the paper properly documents sourcing and ethical mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag Results Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect results-related problems such as poor statistical rigor or overclaiming of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether evaluation is statistically sound, whether baselines are appropriate, whether claims are supported by results (avoid overclaiming), and whether uncertainty and limits of generalization are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag General Presentation and Scope Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify general paper weaknesses like unclear contributions, weak related work, or poor organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the paper clearly states its contributions, situates itself in prior work appropriately, has coherent organization, and contains sufficient clarity for readers to evaluate the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Soundness and Appropriate Scope (critical standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be technically sound and appropriately scoped for the venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the technical claims are correct or sufficiently supported and whether the paper's scope (e.g., empirical vs. theoretical contribution) matches venue expectations. Use these considerations when recommending accept/reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality is absolute—no submission details shared publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose submission contents, results, or identities outside the private review system; treat drafts as confidential until publication and do not discuss them in public fora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI Use Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers cannot use AI to draft reviews or upload confidential materials to non-private services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not input submission text or confidential content into external generative-AI services or use such tools to compose reviews; if AI tools are used at all, follow explicit policy and ensure confidentiality is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind Review / Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not deliberately identify authors before reading; preserve anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid searching for authors or taking actions intended to de-anonymize submissions prior to forming an independent assessment. If anonymity is broken inadvertently, follow policy and report it as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Review Focus
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing resubmissions, focus on whether previous weaknesses were adequately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the submission to prior versions and assess whether authors have meaningfully fixed the issues raised previously rather than re-evaluating from scratch without considering prior critiques.
